text:
TBL arrives on a three-game winning streak, the latest a 6-2 win at VGK that ended the Golden Knights' three-game run. It is game two of a three-game road trip, and the Lightning are 1-0-0 on it. COL comes in off a 4-3 loss at NJD and is 2-2-1 in its last five, playing without Nicolas Roy and Zachary L'Heureux. Both teams have had two days of rest.

The chance numbers are close. At five on five, TBL has taken 57% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side gets) and COL 54%, so there isn't much between them. COL has the better power play numbers (0.7 expected goals per game against 0.62) and the tougher penalty kill (0.43 allowed against 0.57). Our model has it nearly even: 3.1 expected goals for TBL, 3.05 for COL.

In net, projected starter Andrei Vasilevskiy sits at +1.7 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots should allow) this season, after +23.15 last year. COL's projected starter, Mackenzie Blackwood, is at -2.0 this season and was +8.01 last year.

Watch Nikita Kucherov (81% to record a point) and Brandon Hagel (43% to score) for TBL, and Nathan MacKinnon (84% for a point) and Artturi Lehkonen for COL. Lehkonen has 11 points in his last ten games. Anthony Cirelli is one assist from 200 for his career. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Nazem Kadri of COL, at 55% for a point, above his season pace of 49%, because his line creates chances.
